title: AI-Generated Menu Pictures Scare Customers Away
paragraphs: Pictures of food on a menu are meant to make you feel hungry. But some restaurants are finding that AI-generated pictures can have the opposite effect.
It's no surprise that AI-generated and AI-edited food pictures are starting to appear in ads and on restaurant menus — traditional photography and graphic design can be expensive!
Many restaurants are already experimenting with AI. A 2026 report from the US National Restaurant Association found that 26% of restaurant operators were already using AI, including for advertising.
But not everyone likes seeing AI on the menu.
When Grind & Unwind, a cafe in San Francisco, put up a sign showing AI-generated pictures of its menu items, people weren't happy.
Reddit users made fun of the pictures, with one saying the bread looked like reptile skin, and another saying they'd rather see bad photos of real food than bad AI images.
And then, within two days of the photos going viral, the front of the store was covered with graffiti.
The cafe quickly removed the signs — which had been intended to be temporary — and painted over the graffiti, at an estimated cost of more than $700, according to SFGate.
And it's not just in San Francisco. People have been going on X to share "scary," "horrifying" and "disgusting" AI food images from menus and signs across America.
Even when an AI image looks good, just knowing how it was made can change how people see it.
A 2024 study by researchers from the UK and Italy looked at how people reacted to AI-generated pictures of food.
It found that people generally preferred the pictures when they didn't know they were made by a computer. But after they were told that AI had created them, they found them less appealing.
So while AI offers restaurants a cheap way to advertise their food, if those images just make diners lose their appetite, there's no point in using them!
